setlist.title: It's All Over Now, Baby Blue

liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Jack Straw** (2 reviews): Reviewer thinks the opening Jack Straw may be their favorite version ever; Reviewer arrived late, just as Bob sang the line about playing for silver and now for life [15][20]
- **West L.A. Fade Away** (2 reviews): Reviewer names West L.A. the first set's high point; Reviewer calls this the hottest West L.A. ever [18][25]
- **Happy Birthday, Brent** (2 reviews): Bobby's birthday spoof for Brent, though Brent's real birthday is in October; A 15-year-old attendee named Brent was amazed when the band sang happy birthday to Brent [16][24]
- **Samson and Delilah** (2 reviews): Bobby dedicated Samson to the crumbling old Garden, which stood another 11 years; Outstanding Samson; from the rafters the reviewer thought the building would come down, and loved Bobby's closing remark [15][22]
- **Throwing Stones** (2 reviews): Crowd seemed puzzled by Throwing Stones, which was brand new then; Reviewer's first time seeing Throwing Stones live [20][22]
- **Far From Me** (1 review): Brent shows off on a very cool Far From Me [15]
- **It's All Over Now, Baby Blue** (1 review): Baby Blue made a fabulous encore [22]

## Setlist highlights

- **Happy Birthday, Brent**: earliest performance in the archive; mythic rare: 2 archived performances [26]
- **Watchtower Jam**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [26]

## The recordings

- **gd82-09-18.sbd.weise.3153.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): soundboard; 23 songs; 140 min; rated 3.79/5 by 19 [1]. Said about its sound: Nice soundboard, though Phil is somewhat low in the mix in places; Reviewer finds this soundboard thin, lacking ambient sound, with toy-like drums; Earlier audience tapes of this show sounded flat and awful; this soundboard is pristine by comparison [18][21][24]
- **gd1982-09-18.150788.mtx.seamons.ht124.flac16**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 21 songs; 139 min; rated 5/5 by 1 [3]. Said about its sound: Each source was EQ'd with a 31-band equalizer; second set sounded slightly less optimal before EQ work [3]
- **gd1982-09-18.150660.aud.cm.miller.flac16**: audience recording; 21 songs; 139 min [4]
- **gd1982-09-18.150624.eBay.miller.flac2496**: audience recording; 21 songs; 139 min [5]
- **gd1982-09-18.nak300.friend.andrewf.97590.flac16**: source not stated; 21 songs; 144 min; rated 4.67/5 by 3 [12]. Said about its sound: This audience recording is preferred over the soundboard, which the reviewer finds lacking soul [25]

## Around the show

- Reviewer stayed at the Parker House, near the Garden, and saw band instruments arriving, including a guitar tagged 'precious' [17]
- Reviewer was born that night at Brigham & Women's hospital nearby, around the time of The Wheel [23]
- At another show the reviewer attended, Bobby did a similar spoof, claiming it was both drummers' birthdays [16]
- Reviewer calls this show overlooked next to the Portland show the night before and the MSG shows after [21]
- Dupree's Diamond Blues was played three shows in a row: 09/17, 09/18 and 09/20 [25]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd82-09-18.sbd.weise.3153.sbeok.shnf**: source: Soundboard [1]. Also: Soundboard to Dolby cassette to CD, via Michael K. Weise; reported upgrade over the earlier circulating shn set [1]
- **gd1982-09-18.150788.mtx.seamons.ht124.flac16**: transferred by Matrix by Hunter Seamons; source: Matrix by Hunter Seamons using Final Cut Pro (FLAC > AIFF > Final Cut > Soundtrack Pro > AIFF CD tracking via Audacity > FLAC16 via xACT w/meta-tagging) [3]. Also: Matrix of soundboard and audience sources; extra cassette generation likely caused small soundboard hiccups, which were left in [3]
- **gd1982-09-18.150660.aud.cm.miller.flac16**: taped by Unknown; transferred by All Transfers and Mastering By Charlie Miller  September 26, 2020; source: AUD > Cassette Master [4]. Also: Tapes bought on eBay from an estate, source unconfirmed; patch source credited to Bob Morris [4]
- **gd1982-09-18.150624.eBay.miller.flac2496**: taped by Unknown; transferred by All Transfers and Mastering By Charlie Miller  September 26, 2020; source: AUD > Cassette Master [5]. Also: Tapes bought on eBay from an estate, source unconfirmed; patch source credited to Bob Morris [5]
- **gd1982-09-18.nak300.friend.andrewf.97590.flac16**: taped by Tim Friend; transferred by Andrew F.; source: 2x Nakamichi CM300's with CP4 shotguns (L R), plus 1x Nakamichi CM300 with CP1 cardioid (blend mic) > Nakamichi 550 > Maxell XLII-S 90's. Mics on stand, set up… [12]
